title: From Water to Baptism
blurb: Trace the waters of Scripture from creation and the flood to the Jordan, and see why the Church reads them as signs of baptism.

steps.title: The Spirit over the waters
steps.intro: Scripture opens with the Spirit hovering over the waters and God's word bringing order and life out of the deep. The Church has long seen here the first sign of the water that will later bring new birth.

quote.text: For Thy good Spirit indeed was borne over the waters, not borne up by them, as if He rested upon them.

steps.question: What area of your life feels formless, and what would it mean to invite God's Spirit into it?

steps.title: The flood and the dove
steps.intro: After the flood Noah sends out a raven and then a dove, which returns with an olive leaf. The New Testament reads the saving of Noah's household through water as a figure of baptism (1 Peter 3:20-21).

quote.text: The dove is that in the form of which the Holy Spirit descended, as you have read in the New Testament, Who inspires in you peace of soul and tranquillity of mind.

steps.question: What 'olive leaf' of hope has God given you after a hard season?

steps.title: Through the sea on dry ground
steps.intro: Israel passes through the divided waters of the Red Sea and is delivered from slavery in Egypt. Paul says the people were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea (1 Corinthians 10:1-2).

quote.text: For we all were brought out of the land of Egypt, we have all passed through the Red Sea; our enemies pursuing us have perished in the water.

steps.question: What 'Egypt' has God brought you out of, and what still pursues you?

steps.title: Naaman washes in the Jordan
steps.intro: Naaman, a commander afflicted with leprosy, is told by Elisha to wash seven times in the Jordan. He is angry at first, but obeys the humble instruction and is made clean.

quote.text: And being forthwith cleansed, he understood that it is not of the waters but of grace that a man is cleansed.

steps.question: Where might God be asking you to do something simple that your pride resists?

steps.title: Jesus in the Jordan
steps.intro: Jesus comes to John at the Jordan and is baptized. The heavens open, the Spirit descends like a dove, and the Father's voice names him his beloved Son.

quote.text: The heavenly ranks were silent as they stood,—and the Bridegroom went down into Jordan;—the Holy One was baptized and straightway went up,—and His Light shone forth on the world.

steps.question: What does it mean to you that Jesus entered the same waters he would later give to others?

steps.title: Born of water and the Spirit
steps.intro: Nicodemus comes to Jesus by night, and Jesus tells him that no one can enter the kingdom of God without being born of water and the Spirit. The Church has traditionally understood this as a reference to baptism.

quote.text: And in what way are we saved? Plainly because we were regenerate through the grace given in our baptism.

steps.question: How would you describe, in your own words, what it means to be born again?

steps.title: Buried and raised with Christ
steps.intro: Paul explains that baptism unites believers to Christ's death and resurrection, so that they may walk in newness of life. The old self is buried, and a new life begins.

quote.text: Again thou wast asked, Dost thou believe in our Lord Jesus Christ and in His Cross? Thou saidst, I believe, and dippedst thyself; therefore thou wast buried with Christ also: for he who is buried with Christ, rises again with Christ.

steps.question: What would 'walking in newness of life' change in your habits or relationships?
